origins.section: A Method Starts in the Interpreter and Is Compiled in Tiers Once Its Counters Say It Is Hot
Until the Compiled Code Is Installed, the Same Loop Runs Tens of Times Slower
Compiled Code Rests on Assumptions, and a Class Loaded Later Can Make It Not Entrant
A Benchmark Measures Nothing When the JIT Can Drop the Work or Fold Its Input

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-retired-tier: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retired-tier: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-retired-tier: Lines 74-78: "made not entrant" does not mean something failed. Compile 7, the tier-3 score, was made not entrant a millisecond after compile 8 installed tier 4: new calls stop entering the old code and go to the new one ... What tells them apart is whether a newer compile of the same method was already taking calls. The stem has the same pattern as compiles 7 and 8 (tier 3, then tier 4, then the tier-3 code made not entrant).
recorded.prompt:q-second-round: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-round: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-second-round: Lines 116-127: round 2 of the default runs is no faster than round 1. C2's OSR loop compile 11 was made not entrant when round 1 left its loop (unstable_if at the loop's exit test). C2 had compiled no code for leaving the loop, only a trap. Round 2 started in the tier-3 code (compile 10) until the new compiles 130/131. The stem's 9/11/4/4/4 timings match the default runs on lines 104-108.
recorded.prompt:q-plugin-load: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-plugin-load: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-plugin-load: Lines 133-135: when Fee.apply has one implementation, C2 calls it directly, inlines it and records a dependency: if a class that overrides apply is loaded, this code is wrong. Lines 165-173: loading WaivedFee (never called) made both tier-4 compiles of total not entrant at 89 ms, and C2 recompiled. Summary line 275-277 agrees.
recorded.prompt:q-folded-input: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-folded-input: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-folded-input: Lines 254-255: constantInput uses every result and still costs nothing, because mix(42) has the same value on every iteration, so C2 folded it to a constant while compiling. That is 0.01 ns/call by default against about 18 ns/call under -Xint (lines 236-248). The stem matches this case.

recorded.prompt:q-retired-tier:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retired-tier:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-retired-tier:b: Same passage (lines 74-78): a lower tier made not entrant after a newer compile is installed is a replacement, and calls go to the new code, not to the interpreter. Summary: "made not entrant" on a lower tier is usually a replacement.
recorded.prompt:q-retired-tier:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retired-tier:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-retired-tier:c: Lines 81-82 and the Reference (line 293-294): a loop compile is a `%` line with `@ bci`. Compile 91 has neither, so it is an ordinary compile. Also score's tier-4 compile 8 (no %) took its calls.
recorded.prompt:q-retired-tier:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retired-tier:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-retired-tier:d: Lines 76-78: the log prints the same words when code is thrown away because an assumption broke. What tells them apart is whether a newer compile was already taking calls, and compile 91 was. Minor: the "says" adds 'only a compile with nothing newer to take its place sends calls back', which the page implies but does not state.
recorded.prompt:q-second-round:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-round:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-second-round:b: Lines 66-67: tier 3 is C1 code that keeps counting and records branches and types; tier 4 is what C2 compiled from that profile. Reference table: tier 3 'full profiling', tier 4 'C2, from the profile'. The page never says outright that C2 does not profile, but the tier description makes clear that profiling happens in tier 3.
recorded.prompt:q-second-round:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-round:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-second-round:c: Lines 15-16: the interpreter counts calls and loop iterations. Lines 80-83: an OSR compile lets a running call jump into machine code mid-loop. Line 126: round 2 started in tier-3 code, not the interpreter.
recorded.prompt:q-second-round:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-second-round:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-second-round:d: Lines 67-69 and the Reference table: tier 1 is plain C1 code without profiling, given to a trivial method that only returns a field (Weights::factor). round went through tier 3 (compile 10) to tier 4.
recorded.prompt:q-plugin-load:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-plugin-load:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-plugin-load:b: Lines 175-180: the receiver-class check, invalidated only at the first call with the new class, is what happened with LateInterface, where Fee was an interface with final implementations. With Fee as a class, the load alone invalidated the code (line 171).
recorded.prompt:q-plugin-load:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-plugin-load:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-plugin-load:c: Line 143: WaivedFee was 'loaded in round 6, never called', and line 171 says loading it invalidated both tier-4 compiles of total.
recorded.prompt:q-plugin-load:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-plugin-load:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-plugin-load:d: Lines 165-166, 171: the load made total's tier-4 code not entrant at 89 ms. Design Note lines 334-335: the JVM can throw away compiled code (dependencies on the class hierarchy, traps, interpreter fallback).
recorded.prompt:q-folded-input:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-folded-input:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-folded-input:b: Lines 252-255 and 258-259: removal as unused work is the discarded case, where nothing used the result. A sum that is returned and printed counts as consuming the results (the result reaches something the JIT can't see through), and constantInput uses every result yet costs nothing because its input is constant.
recorded.prompt:q-folded-input:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-folded-input:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-folded-input:c: Lines 254-255: 'constantInput uses every result, and still costs nothing'. Lines 258-260: a measurement can be trusted only when results are consumed AND inputs vary. The cost of the hash itself is consumed's 0.41 ns, not 0.01.
recorded.prompt:q-folded-input:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-folded-input:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-folded-input:d: Line 6: 0.01 ns per call is less than one CPU cycle. Lines 233-237: consumed compiled costs 0.41 ns, so 0.01 is not the compiled cost of the work. Lines 262-263: -Xint shows how much work there was. Minor: the "says" claims interpreter overhead explains part of the gap. The page shows that with numbers (18 ns vs 0.41 ns) but never states it.
